source.publication: 2025 Expanded Instructions (IA 1040) and the 2025 IA 1040 Iowa Individual Income Tax Return
source.section: IA 1040 form PDF p.1 Step 3 lines a, b, d; form PDF p.2 lines 1c, 2-5, 7, 8, 11, 12; Instructions PDF p.8 Step 3; PDF p.9-10 lines 2-4; PDF p.12 line 5 ('Iowa now has a flat tax rate of 3.8%'); PDF p.18 line 12

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (you) 50,000.00 + wages (spouse) 30,000.00 = 80,000.00. Federal taxable income = 80,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 48,500.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). IA 1040 filing status 2 (married filing jointly). Step 3 line a personal credits 2 x 40.00 = 80.00; line b 0 x 20.00 = 0.00 (65 or older on or before January 1, 2026; nobody blind); line c no dependents; line d and line 8 = 80.00. Line 1c federal AGI 80,000.00; line 2 federal taxable income 48,500.00. Schedule 1: no additions or subtractions. Schedule 1 line 21 net modifications = 0.00; line 3 = 0.00. Line 4 Iowa taxable income = 48,500.00 + (0.00) = 48,500.00. Line 5 tax = 3.8% x 48,500.00 = 1,843.00; line 7 = 1,843.00. Line 11 total credits 80.00; line 12 balance = 1,843.00 - 80.00 = 1,763.00. State income tax 1,763.00 (no line 13-17 credits; line 19 school district or EMS surtax is local, not computed). The form allows whole-dollar rounding; expected keeps the cents. Low-income exemption and alternate tax (PDF p.10-13): line 4 48,500.00 + federal deduction 31,500.00 = 80,000.00, against 13,500.00: not exempt; alternate tax 4.3% x (80,000.00 - 13,500.00) = 2,859.50, not smaller than the 3.8% tax.
accepted_approximations: School district and county EMS surtaxes (a percentage of the tax, form line 19) are local and out of scope (issue #1).
